newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli bonds close higher in quiet trading.
newsitem.headline: Israeli bonds close higher in quiet trading.

text.p: Israeli bonds closed higher on Sunday in quiet trading as the market regained its composure after last week's unexpectedly high consumer price index, traders said.
Indices:
* Government bonds general: +0.07 pct to 100.04
* CPI-linked government bonds: +0.13 pct to 100.03
* Unlinked government bonds: +0.11 pct to 109.73
* Dollar-linked government bonds: -0.35 pct to 110.98
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.07 pct to 107.94
Volume including Makams was a low 125 million shekels.

"The market was quiet today after the big step it took last week on the high CPI. Now the market is stable and should stay at these levels for the near term," said Ron Weisberg of IBI Investment House.
"The market is now waiting to see what will happen to interest rates at the end of the month and also to see what July's CPI will be. Only then will it develop new expectations," Weisberg said.

He said he did not believe the central bank would raise August interest rates when it announced its monthly monetary programme July 28. The Bank of Israel slashed its base lending rate in mid-June by 1.2 percentage points to an annualised 12.7 percent.
June's CPI, published last week, rose by an unexpectedly high 1.1 percent. The rise was due mainly to housing prices and many analysts are predicting a high index in July as well.
The high index caused prices of CPI-linked bonds to rise and unlinked bonds to fall last week. But on Sunday unlinked bonds reversed course.
"Unlinked bonds today underwent a correction on their falls of last week. With yields around 13 percent, traders are willing to buy," said Weisberg.
"The next CPI is crucial. If it continues to be high (in July) then unlinked bond prices will fall again," said Eyal Segal of United Mizrahi Bank.

CPI-linked bonds continued higher on Sunday, which Segal said was due to a tightening supply in the market. "Redemptions are bigger than new issues, which has created a concerns about a shortage," he said.

"The yield curve of CPI-linked bonds is normal again, with a premium for long bonds. CPI-linked floaters had a good rise today, because there are some fears in the market that interest rates will go up in future because of a stronger dollar," Weisberg said.
Dollar-linked bonds fell on Sunday after the dollar weakened against the shekel on Friday. The representative rate of the dollar was fixed at 3.5320 shekels against 3.5520 on Thursday.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
($1=3.53 shekels)
